body:
DO NOT SUPERSEDE BUG-1476 YET. I recommended it this afternoon and the evidence has just turned against me. The code-identity argument was sound; the conclusion I drew from it was not.

STORY-1350 RAN ON THE NEW BINARY TWENTY MINUTES AGO AND DID THE EXACT THING BUG-1476 DESCRIBES:

    23:13:28  PhaseEntered implementer
    23:13:49  PhaseEntered ci          <- 21 seconds
    23:13:52  PhaseEntered reviewer    <- 3 seconds
    23:19:00  SpecShelved verdict:request-changes

    branch tip: 0c09fe8e2c, committed 2026-09-19 21:46 — NO new commit

Wave binary is b09197ab72, which I verified contains BUG-1445's merge. So the guard is in the running code and the no-op round happened anyway: twenty-one seconds, no commit, a three-second CI phase reading a cached result for an unmoved head, then a full reviewer cycle re-reaching the same conclusion. That is BUG-1476's description verbatim, on the fix that was supposed to have made it redundant.

WHAT I AM CLAIMING AND WHAT I AM NOT. Observed: the sequence above, from events.jsonl and git. Not diagnosed: why the guard did not fire. I can see it arms at lib.rs:87220 behind `blocking_rework_verdict(..)` returning a blocking verdict and `pr_head_sha_best_effort` returning a head, and that `PR-1974.json` held a CHANGES REQUESTED verdict throughout — so it looks like it should have armed. It did not stop the run. I have not read far enough to say whether it failed to arm, armed and was not consulted, or was consulted in a phase that had already been entered. Five of my causal claims needed correcting today and I am not adding a sixth.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS, and it is the lesson for me. The reviewer established that #2029's production change is redundant — same function, same call site, already on main. That is TRUE and I verified it myself. What I then did was treat "the code is already there" as equivalent to "the spec's acceptance is met". It is not. BUG-1476's acceptance is that the DEFECT STOPS HAPPENING, and twenty minutes ago it happened.

So both can hold: #2029 has nothing to contribute, AND BUG-1476 should stay open because what it describes is live.

SUGGESTED, though disposition is yours:

  - Close PR #2029 — the reviewer's call-site finding settles that it adds nothing. My salvage
    of its one negative test is PR #2036, falsifiability verified by breaking the guard and
    showing it red.
  - Keep BUG-1476 OPEN rather than superseding, with STORY-1350's 23:13 run appended as
    post-BUG-1445 evidence. Its acceptance is unmet.
  - BUG-1495's dependency question reopens with it. You unblocked BUG-1495 on my argument that
    the guard was live and working. The guard is live; "working" is now in doubt.

I would rather hand you a reversal than let a spec be superseded because I stopped checking at the code.
